items.reason: Pinning an action to a SHA means asking GitHub what a tag points at right now, and this session has no network; the repo already has scripts/actions-pin.mjs --update, which resolves every tag AND flips its own STRICT/RATCHET in the same pass, so the close is one networked command plus the ledger floor.

The rule, the checker (scripts/commit-subject.mjs, rubric A5) and the provenance trailers all exist and run in .husky/prepare-commit-msg; what breaks it is an outer lane harness committing its report's first line in a throwaway worktree with no hooks installed, which is not fixable from inside the repository and not measurable here without git history.

Already covered: .github/guidance-budget.json declares the seven READ-FIRST documents with a per-file and total line ceiling (AGENTS.md 934, total 1602), npm run guidance:budget prints it and test-unit/guidance-budget.test.mjs blocks on every build; I deliberately added no line to AGENTS.md or docs/task-index.md, both of which sit exactly on their ceilings.

Found and fenced three unquarantined third-party surfaces (fetched page text in onboarding-scan, public review quotes in local-page, scan-derived profile prose in channel-research), added four adversarial corpus cases that exercise them, and added a census that enumerates every prompt builder so a fourth cannot arrive unnoticed.

A staged rollout on Vercel is platform configuration (skew protection, alias promotion) plus a token that can move a deployment, and .github/workflows/post-deploy.yml already argues in writing that arming an automatic abort is the operator's decision because it needs a token that can write master; the repository half (a dated, automatic health verdict after every release) is already there.

Already covered: test-llm/model-pins.json pins the model surface every golden/budget/bake was accepted against, test-llm/model-candidates.json declares the successor, npm run llm:candidate rehearses every registered operation against it through the real wrapper weekly in llm-drift.yml, and test-unit/model-candidate-census.test.mjs blocks when a candidate row stops naming the model actually being served.

scripts/setup-walk.mjs now follows docs/open-source/self-hosting.md § Quick start on a clean machine (asserts the page still gives the commands, copies .env.example, builds under SELF_HOSTED+LOCAL_DB, boots and fetches /, parses the compose file) and .github/workflows/setup-walk.yml runs it weekly and on every change to the files it walks, keeping a dated verdict for 90 days.

Already covered: .github/constraint-map.json is exactly that artefact — one row per never/always rule AGENTS.md states, with a rung of blocking | reporting | partial | honour, a mitigation field on the honour rows and a gapNote on the partial ones, summarised as a table in AGENTS.md and held to the tree (and to the check:ci chain) by test-unit/constraint-map.test.mjs.

lessons: In this repository every fence is paired with a pin, a ceiling or a census, and the meta-tests enforce the pairing: adding an exception without its ceiling, a check:ci stage without a constraint-map row, or a line to AGENTS.md without raising .github/guidance-budget.json all turn the unit suite red. Read the pin file before the source file — the two-line diff is the house style, and half of one is a red build.

The scan's 'missing' bullets are worth verifying before acting on them: three of eight items here (guidance budget, model-candidate rehearsal, the unfenced-rule map) were already implemented as first-class artefacts with blocking tests, and the honest move was to name the artefact rather than build a second one next to it.

A prompt-injection corpus can only cover the builders somebody remembered. Enumerating the builders instead — every module under the AI seam, with the ORIGIN of the text it renders — is what found three unfenced third-party surfaces that eight hand-written adversarial cases had walked past for months.
